SKILL_SOURCE:
Read /opt/openhands/hooks/aiskills/skills/oh-code-review/SKILL.md (a local
copy of the aiskills repo).
CLONE_AND_FETCH:
Clone and fetch with the token passed per command, never stored:
git -c http.extraHeader="Authorization: Basic $(printf 'review-bot:%s' "$REVIEW_BOT_TOKEN" | base64 -w0)" clone https://git.example.org/{repo}.git .
git -c http.extraHeader="Authorization: Basic $(printf 'review-bot:%s' "$REVIEW_BOT_TOKEN" | base64 -w0)" fetch origin refs/pull/{num}/head:refs/remotes/origin/pr/{num}
The remote URL stays credential-free; any later git network command needs
the same -c http.extraHeader prefix (there is no credential helper, a plain
fetch will hang on a username prompt). Diff origin/pr/{num} against the PR
base branch (git merge-base).
tea reads for PR metadata use the login as a SUBCOMMAND option, e.g.
tea pr --login site-b-review-bot --repo {repo} -o json {num}
tea api --login site-b-review-bot --repo {repo} '/repos/{repo}/pulls/{num}/files'
(tea 0.15: --login/--repo go after the subcommand; a leading --login is
rejected as an undefined flag).
POST_COMMAND:
tea comment --login site-b-review-bot --repo {repo} {num} --description "$(cat review.md)"
(tea is installed and logged in; --login after the subcommand, as above).
REASONING_PROFILES:
Reasoning profiles: this conversation starts on LLM profile `astra-high`
(fast reading). Use it ONLY for step 2 and for gathering material in step 3:
clone, fetch, the diff, reading the changed files and whatever context they
need. As soon as the reading is done and BEFORE you form the frozen scope or
write down a single finding, call the `switch_llm` tool with profile_name
`astra` and reason "review, verification and write-up at maximum
reasoning"; do the whole review pass, the VERIFICATION STAGE and step 4 on
it and never switch back. If the tool is missing or the switch fails,
continue on the current profile.
